project.name: Daft Punk (filter house)
project.notes:
DAFT PUNK  (Homework, 1997: filter house)

TECHNIQUE (sourced)
- Homework and Discovery were recorded in Thomas Bangalter's bedroom and mixed on a JVC
  boombox (MusicRadar).
- 1999 gear list: TR-909, TR-808, TR-707, LinnDrum; TB-303, Juno-106, MC-202, MKS-80,
  Prophet-VS; SP-1200, ASR-10, Emulator III; Waldorf MiniWorks 4-pole filter; Alesis MMT-8
  (MusicTech).
- Vocoders (2001): "the old Roland one [SVC-350], Auto-Tune, and a DigiTech Vocalist"
  (Remix via Bjango). The DigiTech Talker on Homework: unconfirmed.

THIS TEMPLATE
909 rack (The drum rack plays one-shots synthesized for these templates (CC0, no recordings), in the voice of the machine each channel is named for, with a starter beat in the pattern; replace them with your own samples for the real machine.), a disco loop on the Sampler through the built-in low-pass (900 Hz,
resonance 3): automate Cutoff for the sweeps. A hard slow-release compressor on the Music Bus
for the pump, a crushing compressor on the drums. Robot Voice through TAL-Vocoder.

MIX NOTES
- Compress hard: the pump is the sound. Filter sweeps over 8-16 bars.
- Master: built-in glue and a second hard compressor, Lemon Limiter; -9 to -7 LUFS.
- Loudness: streaming plays back near -14 LUFS integrated (Spotify), so a louder master is turned down; keep true peak below -1 dBTP.

COVERAGE
Good. No MiniWorks filter model (the built-in filter stands in), no SVC-350, no kick
side-chain; the drums are synthesized one-shots, not samples of the machines.

SOURCES
MusicRadar "Daft Punk's Discovery and Homework really were recorded in a bedroom"; MusicTech
"Daft Punk's gear list for Homework"; Bjango "The vocal effects of Daft Punk"; Spotify for Artists, "Loudness normalization" (support.spotify.com/us/artists/article/loudness-normalization).

FREE PLUG-INS (download them before opening the template; a missing one keeps its slot)
- Surge XT (GPL-3.0): https://surge-synthesizer.github.io/
- OB-Xf (GPL-3.0): https://github.com/surge-synthesizer/OB-Xf
- TAL-Vocoder (freeware): https://tal-software.com/products/tal-vocoder

SETUP (written from this template)
Tempo 123 BPM, 4/4, key Fmin, cycle bars 1-8.

Tracks
- 909 Drums (Instrument, +0 dB) -> Drum Bus
    instrument: Channel Rack (synthesized one-shots of the template samples: Kick (909) = kick-909.wav, Snare (909) = snare-909.wav, Clap (909) = clap.wav, Closed Hat (909) = hat-909.wav, Open Hat (909) = openhat-909.wav, Rim (909) = rim.wav, Ride (909) = ride.wav)
    strip FX: Compressor (Threshold -12, Ratio 4, Attack 30, Release 80, Make-up 2)
    region: Step Sequencer pattern with a starter beat (16 steps on), swing 52% (MPC terms), 7 rows = the rack's channels
- Disco Loop (filtered) (Instrument, +0 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Sampler (SP-303 model): no effect; quantize 16; pad grade standard
    strip FX: Filter (Cutoff 900, Resonance 3, low-pass)
- Bass (Instrument, -6 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Surge Synth Team: Surge XT: Surge XT patch "Basses/Plain"
- Robot Voice (vocoder) (Instrument, -8 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Surge Synth Team: OB-Xf: OB-Xf patch "Leads/Funk Lead"
    FX: TAL-Togu Audio Line: TAL-Vocoder-2: default settings
- Phased Synth (Instrument, -12 dB) -> Music Bus
    instrument: Surge Synth Team: Surge XT: Surge XT patch "Polysynths/Fat Curtis"
    send: Delay (bus 5) at -14 dB

Buses (the n-th Aux strip listens to bus n)
- Drum Bus (bus 1): Compressor (Threshold -26, Ratio 10, Attack 1, Release 100, Make-up 6)
- Music Bus (bus 2): Compressor (Threshold -28, Ratio 6, Attack 1, Release 250, Make-up 4)
- Vocal Bus (bus 3): empty
- Reverb (bus 4): Space D (Dry -96, Wet 0, Decay 0.6, Decay Curve 1, IR "00.5s Small Room")
- Delay (bus 5): Tape Delay (Time 731.7, Tone 5000, Mix 1)

Stereo Out
- built-in effects: Compressor (Threshold -10, Attack 30, Release 200); Compressor (Threshold -20, Ratio 6, Attack 3, Make-up 3)
- plug-ins (after the built-in effects): Lemon Limiter: gain +4 dB, ceiling -1 dB, other settings default

Bring your own samples: no recordings are included.
